A0222.title: Targeted Inspection
A0222.definition: Rule-based targeted inspection of high-risk merchants, sites, or courier tasks to verify consistency between physical goods and system data.
A0222.description:
Targeted inspection uses risk scores, historical anomalies, and scenario features to trigger manual or system inspection of suspected merchants and courier pickup/delivery tasks, verifying that goods, weight, route, and sign-off match system data.

It addresses data-distortion risks such as weight shaving, fake routing, and heavy-goods splitting, following a "data anomaly → targeted verification → closed-loop handling" workflow that requires evidence and appeal mechanisms to avoid false positives.
A0222.limitation: Inspection coverage is limited and depends on risk-score quality and sample representativeness; high-frequency inspection affects fulfillment efficiency and merchant experience, requiring a balance between sampling rate and false-positive cost.

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 AU-6 Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting

A0222-001.title: Trusted-Merchant Targeted Inspection
A0222-001.definition: Low-frequency targeted inspection of trusted-list merchants to verify fulfillment goods and declaration consistency.
A0222-001.description:
Trusted merchants typically enjoy inspection-free or fast-track benefits; targeted inspection uses low-frequency sampling to verify that trust is not abused, focusing on goods consistency, weight, and category declarations matching orders.

It safeguards trusted-merchant fulfillment efficiency while identifying fake shipment, swaps, or false declarations under trust qualification, following a "trust admission + sampling review + trust downgrade" workflow.
A0222-001.limitation: Low-frequency sampling has limited capture rate for single violations and requires complaint and anomaly triggers for additional sampling; the feedback loop from inspection results to trust rating must be closed.

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 AU-6 Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting

A0222-002.title: Courier Targeted Inspection Task
A0222-002.definition: Dispatching targeted inspection tasks for high-risk courier pickup/delivery tasks to verify weight, route, and sign-off authenticity.
A0222-002.description:
For weight shaving, fake routing, and fake handover risks, targeted inspection tasks are dispatched by task-level risk scores, with quality-control or risk staff performing on-site or system verification of billed weight, node trajectories, and sign-off data against declarations.

It pushes inspection down to per-task granularity for timely interception of data falsification during fulfillment, following a "task scoring → targeted dispatch → on-site verification → accountability" workflow.
A0222-002.limitation: On-site inspection is labor-intensive and depends on task risk-score accuracy; cross-site and cross-partner tasks require coordinated verification permissions.

references.title: NIST SP 800-53 AU-6 Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
